_: Reference profile, extracted from radix-ui/themes (MIT) so that every number in
this repository can be re-derived from public code by anybody.
Facts — exports, props, what each renders — are extracted. Level, surface and the
description are AUTHORED here, as the worked example of the tier no library ships.
They are one person's reading of a public library, not the library's own words.

Avatar.description: A person or a team as an image with a letter fallback. Presentational: it knows nothing about presence or status — pair it with Badge if that has to show.

Badge.description: A small standalone pill that labels state. Not Kbd, which shows a key to press, and not Code, which shows a literal.

BaseButton.description: The unstyled button every other button is built on. Reach for Button; this is here to be extended, not used.
BaseButton.exampleIs: extracted from the best real usage in this repository; nothing maintains it, and it records how the component is used today rather than how it should be

Blockquote.description: A quoted passage set apart from the text around it. Quote marks a phrase inline; this takes the whole block.

Box.description: A div with the token system attached and no opinion of its own. Use it when nothing more specific fits — reaching for it often means a component is missing.
Box.example:
<Box flexGrow="1" p={{ initial: '4', xs: '5' }} position="relative">
              {!!shortcut && (
                <Box position="absolute" top="0" right="0" m="2">
                  {shortcut}
                </Box>
              )}
              <ThemePanelContent onAppearanceChange={onAppearanceChange} context={themeContext} />
            </Box>
Box.exampleIs: extracted from the best real usage in this repository; nothing maintains it, and it records how the component is used today rather than how it should be

Button.description: The main way to start an action. IconButton when the label is the icon; Link when it navigates rather than acts.
Button.exampleIs: extracted from the best real usage in this repository; nothing maintains it, and it records how the component is used today rather than how it should be

Card.description: A bounded surface that groups related content and can be made interactive as a whole. Not Box: a Card is a thing on a page, a Box is a wrapper.

Checkbox.description: One independent yes/no. Switch when the change takes effect immediately; Radio when exactly one of several must be chosen.

CheckboxGroup.description: Several checkboxes sharing one name and one value array. Use it when the set is the field, not the individual boxes.

CheckboxGroupIndicator.description: The mark inside a grouped checkbox. A part, not a component to reach for.

CheckboxGroupItem.description: One box inside a CheckboxGroup. It reads its state from the group and cannot be used alone.

ChevronDownIcon.description: The disclosure chevron used by controls that open. A part of those controls, not a general-purpose icon.
ChevronDownIcon.exampleIs: extracted from the best real usage in this repository; nothing maintains it, and it records how the component is used today rather than how it should be

Code.description: A literal shown as code inline. Kbd for a key the reader should press.

Container.description: Centres content and caps its width. The outermost layout piece on a page; Section divides what is inside it.

Em.description: Stress emphasis, carried semantically. Strong for importance rather than emphasis.

Flex.description: One-dimensional arrangement with the spacing scale attached. Grid when both axes matter.
Flex.example:
<Flex align="center" justify="center" height="32px">
                    <Theme asChild scaling={value}>
                      <Flex align="center" justify="center">
                        <Text size="1" weight="medium">
                          {upperFirst(value)}
                        </Text>
                      </Flex>
                    </Theme>
                  </Flex>
Flex.exampleIs: extracted from the best real usage in this repository; nothing maintains it, and it records how the component is used today rather than how it should be

Grid.description: Two-dimensional arrangement. Flex when only one axis is being controlled.
Grid.exampleIs: extracted from the best real usage in this repository; nothing maintains it, and it records how the component is used today rather than how it should be

Heading.description: A section title with its level carried separately from its size, so the outline stays correct when the visual scale changes.
Heading.exampleIs: extracted from the best real usage in this repository; nothing maintains it, and it records how the component is used today rather than how it should be

IconButton.description: An action whose label is its icon, and which therefore needs an accessible name. Button when there is room for words.

Inset.description: Content that breaks out of its Card padding to meet the edge — an image at the top of a card, and little else.

Kbd.description: A key the reader is being asked to press. Code for a literal value.
Kbd.example:
<Kbd asChild size="3" tabIndex={0} className="rt-ThemePanelShortcut">
              <button
                type="button"
                onClick={() => setOpen((open) => !open)}
                ref={triggerRef}
                aria-label="Toggle the Theme Panel"
              >
                T
              </button>
            </Kbd>
Kbd.exampleIs: extracted from the best real usage in this repository; nothing maintains it, and it records how the component is used today rather than how it should be

Link.description: Navigation. If it changes state rather than location it is a Button, whatever it looks like.

Progress.description: How far along a known-length task is. Spinner when the length is unknown.

Quote.description: A quoted phrase inside running text. Blockquote when the quote is the block.

Radio.description: Exactly one of several. Checkbox when the choices are independent.

Reset.description: Strips a native element back to nothing so it can be styled. Plumbing.

ScrollArea.description: A region that scrolls with consistent scrollbars across platforms. Its presence is a layout decision, not a styling one.
ScrollArea.example:
<ScrollArea>
            <Box flexGrow="1" p={{ initial: '4', xs: '5' }} position="relative">
              {!!shortcut && (
                <Box position="absolute" top="0" right="0" m="2">
                  {shortcut}
                </Box>
              )}
              <ThemePanelContent onAppearanceChange={onAppearanceChange} context={themeContext} />
            </Box>
          </ScrollArea>
ScrollArea.exampleIs: extracted from the best real usage in this repository; nothing maintains it, and it records how the component is used today rather than how it should be

Section.description: A vertical band of a page with the vertical rhythm applied. Container caps the width; this divides the height.

Separator.description: A line that means a break in content, announced as one. A border is decoration; this is structure.

Skeleton.description: The shape of content that has not arrived, holding its space so nothing jumps.

Slider.description: A value chosen from a continuous range by dragging. A number field when the exact value matters more than the feel of it.

Spinner.description: Something is happening and its length is unknown. Progress when it is known.
Spinner.exampleIs: extracted from the best real usage in this repository; nothing maintains it, and it records how the component is used today rather than how it should be

Strong.description: Importance, carried semantically. Em for emphasis rather than importance.

Switch.description: A setting that takes effect the moment it is flipped. Checkbox when the change is submitted later.

Text.description: Body copy with the type scale attached. Heading when it titles a section.
Text.example:
<Text
        as="p"
        size={mapResponsiveProp(size, mapCalloutSizeToTextSize)}
        {...props}
        asChild={false}
        ref={forwardedRef}
        className={classNames('rt-CalloutText', className)}
      />
Text.exampleIs: extracted from the best real usage in this repository; nothing maintains it, and it records how the component is used today rather than how it should be

TextArea.description: Multi-line input. A single-line field when the answer is short — the height is the promise.

Theme.description: The root that carries appearance, accent and radius down the tree. One per application, or one per deliberately different area.
Theme.example:
<Theme asChild>
          <TooltipPrimitive.Content
            sideOffset={4}
            collisionPadding={10}
            {...tooltipContentProps}
            asChild={false}
            ref={forwardedRef}
            className={classNames('rt-TooltipContent', className)}
          >
            <Text as="p" className="rt-TooltipText" size="1">
              {content}
            </Text>
            <TooltipPrimitive.Arrow className="rt-TooltipArrow" />
          </TooltipPrimitive.Content>
        </Theme>

Tooltip.description: A short label revealed on hover or focus, for something already visible. It cannot hold anything interactive — use a popover for that.
Tooltip.example:
<Tooltip content="Press T to show/hide the Theme Panel" side="bottom" sideOffset={6}>
            <Kbd asChild size="3" tabIndex={0} className="rt-ThemePanelShortcut">
              <button
                type="button"
                onClick={() => setOpen((open) => !open)}
                ref={triggerRef}
                aria-label="Toggle the Theme Panel"
              >
                T
              </button>
            </Kbd>
          </Tooltip>
